pr_title: roachprod: reuse start script if start is called with --restart=true
pr_body:
Previously, irrespective of the restart flag value we ended up overwriting the startup script which led to defaulting the values of other flags passed previously to the start command. This was inadequate because when restarting,
i.e., `restart=true`, it makes more sense that we would reuse the existing startup script by default. This patch changes this behaviour.

Epic: none
Fixes: #125085
Release note: None

issue_context.title: roachprod: reuse start script if start is called with --restart=false
issue_context.body:
Currently, if we call `roachprod start <cluster> --restart=false`, we skip init as expected, but we'd overwrite the script `cockroach.sh` on the node with a new script containing new arguments passed into `roachprod start`, if any. One such argument is `--store-count`, which defaults to 1 if unspecified. This makes it really easy to make a mistake where `roachprod stop` and `roachprod start --restart=false` results in the store count dropping from, say, 4 to 1, resulting in most ranges becoming unavailable as they were on one of the non-live stores.

`drtprod start` defaults to running `roachprod start ... --restart=false`, and so it's easy to make this mistake when managing drt clusters. We should reuse (and just run) the startup script if `--restart=false` is passed in, and have an explicit `--overwrite-startup-script` flag or so if we actually want to overwrite `cockroach.sh` with new args.

Jira issue: CRDB-39226
